top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is mature, reproduced for three decades, mechanistically explained (amido-Pd chemistry, beta-hydride elimination, C-N reductive elimination solved by ligand design) and cleanly attributable to Buchwald and Hartwig. It is a distinct achievement from the 2010 C-C coupling prize and is routine in pharmaceutical, materials and total synthesis. Targeted protein degradation is a close second: a clear chemical idea with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as defensible laureates, but less mature since no degrader is approved. Lipid nanoparticles rank third because the citation and laureate allocation remain unsettled. No award ranks last since several candidates are worthy.
